 Micron (MU) Stock Falls 12% in Five Days, but Hedge Funds Keep Buying
 Micron (MU) stock fell 12% in five days, yet trades at 3.8x forward earnings as hedge funds add. HPE, Analog Devices and Marvell report next week. By Maisie Morrison November 20, 2026 No Comments 3 Mins Read

 The Multiples Keep Shrinking 
 Big Funds Bought the Dip 
 Micron (MU) fell 3.2% in premarket trading Friday and is down 12% over five days.
 Micron trades at 3.8 times forward earnings, versus 3.1 for SK Hynix and 2.5 for Samsung.
 Appaloosa raised its Micron stake 28% and Altimeter added 24% in the third quarter.
 The average analyst target implies almost 150% upside from current levels.
 HPE, Analog Devices and Marvell report next week.
 Micron (MU) can’t catch a break. The stock slipped 3.2% in premarket trading on Friday, adding to a 12% drop over the past five days.
Micron Technology, Inc., MU
 SK Hynix is not faring better. Its stock was down 1.3% in early trading after a rough week of its own.
 Anthropic (ANT) went public on Thursday, but the debut did little for chip names. The AI trade is still stuck in a selloff.
 Memory stocks have been under pressure for months. Worries include rising debt, the staying power of AI spending and a leadership crisis at Nvidia (NVDA).
 The Multiples Keep Shrinking 
 Micron now trades at 3.8 times forward earnings. SK Hynix’s US-listed stock sits at 3.1, and Samsung Electronics is at 2.5.
 Many S&P 500 names trade at 15 to 20 times forward earnings. Memory usually sits lower because the business runs in cycles.
 Even so, these readings are low for the group. Micron’s forward multiple swung between 4.5 and above 11 for much of early 2026.
 Some analysts warn against leaning on forward P/E for memory names. Still, Wall Street leans positive on Micron.
 Most analysts rate the stock a Buy. The average price target implies almost 150% upside, per Dow Jones Market Data.
 Big Funds Bought the Dip 
 Quarterly filings show several hedge funds added Micron in the third quarter. The stock fell 7.7% in that stretch, from $1,154.29 on June 30 to $1,065.11 on Sept. 30.
 David Tepper’s Appaloosa Management lifted its position by 28%, to 1.25 million. Altimeter Capital, led by Brad Gerstner, added 24% to reach about 260,000.
 Soros Fund Management moved to almost 36,000 from 22,400. Discovery Capital grew its position to almost 15,000 from 1,400, a more than tenfold jump.
 Not everyone bought. Soros Capital, run by Robert Soros, cut its position by almost 74%, to 9,400 from 36,700.
 The records do not explain why each fund acted. They also do not say where the stock goes next.
 Earnings may offer clues. Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports Monday, and Analog Devices follows on Tuesday.
 Marvell Technology reports Thursday. The three reports should shed light on AI spending trends that bear on Micron and SK Hynix.
